subject: Data Engineering
title: GitLab's Database Deletion
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on GitLab's Database Deletion.

hook.text: A tired GitLab engineer ran a database delete command on the production server instead of the staging one.

buildup.text: In 2017, during a late-night incident, a GitLab admin deleted the production PostgreSQL database.

discovery.text: Five backup methods were in place. None of them worked — they were either stale, misconfigured, or untested.

twist.text: The only working backup was a 6-hour-old staging snapshot. GitLab lost 6 hours of user data permanently.

climax.text: GitLab live-streamed the recovery and published a full post-mortem. Transparency turned disaster into trust.

punchline.text: Five backup methods. Zero that worked. Test your backups.

quiz.question: What lesson did the GitLab database deletion teach?
options: Backups must be regularly tested to confirm they work
Production databases should never have backups
Engineers should never work at night
